thread:
Maria Gonzalez: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector tweak rolled yesterday we’re seeing ~6% drop in observed batch utilization on p4-heavy hosts. I ran a short profile and attached the flame snippet below.

Raj Patel: ugh ok, timeline? which rollout id?

Maria Gonzalez: rollout id rwd/ks/2026-03-17 v1.2.3 — change replaced the heuristic that preferred fused attention kernels for seq_len>512. New selector picks kernel based on median seq distribution instead of worst-case.

Tom Wu: do we have concrete signals? batch_util went down, queue_depth up? other noise?

Maria Gonzalez: quick metrics (from prod-mon):
- batch_utilization p95: 0.72 -> 0.66
- avg_queue_depth: 2.1 -> 3.8
- tokens/sec per-host: -4.8% overall but -9% on p4.

Eva Li: that aligns with the profiler — more small batches formed, more kernel switches per request, and some cross-kernel cache thrash.

Maria Gonzalez: pasted minimal repro PromQL I used:
```promql
sum(rate(redwood_batch_tokens_total[1m])) by (host) / sum(redwood_batch_gpu_capacity) by (host)
```

Raj Patel: can you also dump KV cache hit-rate by host? suspected issue is prefix caching effectiveness dropping when kernel choice changes IO pattern.

Maria Gonzalez: KV cache hit-rate sample: host p4-12: 0.81 -> 0.66 (10:00 -> 11:30 after rollout). Attached small trace showing kvcache misses correlated with microbatch evictions.

Tom Wu: possible root: selector moved to median sequence length; for tails that prefer fused kernel we now pick slower kernel causing slower token stepping and smaller microbatches. That can reduce prefix reuse and increase KV miss amplification.

Eva Li: agree. Short term mitigation: revert selector for models with bimodal seq distribution OR add a secondary policy: if kvcache_hitrate drops >5% in 30m, pin fused kernel.

Raj Patel: can we detect that via telemetry and auto-fallback? i.e. a continuous-batching guardrail that monitors batch_util and kvcache_hitrate and toggles kernel variant when thresholds hit.

Maria Gonzalez: I prototyped a lightweight rule engine in the runtime agent. Pseudoconfig: 
```json
{"rules": [{"if": "kvcache_hitrate < 0.7 and batch_util < 0.7","then": "force_kernel=fused","window": "30m"}]}
```

Tom Wu: that’s promising. Need to be careful with oscillation — add cooldown and require sustained signal. Also track queue RTT to avoid flapping.

Eva Li: suggested metric additions for the dashboard:
- batch_utilization (p50/p95) per-model per-host
- queue_depth and queue_rtt (p50/p95)
- kvcache_hitrate and kvcache_evictions/sec
- token_rate (tokens/sec) and kernel_switches/sec
- a derived "batch_stability" score (0-1) combining queue_rtt and kernel_switches

Maria Gonzalez: example scoreboard query for Grafana panel (tokens/sec by kernel):
```promql
sum by (kernel) (rate(redwood_token_emitted_total[1m]))
```

Raj Patel: can we add a burn-in check when rolling new selector? something like 2h canary and compute delta over baseline with CI to decide cutover.

Maria Gonzalez: yes — new rollout plan:
1) canary 1 host for 30m (collect metrics)
2) canary 10% for 2h (auto-compare against baseline)
3) full rollout with staged ramp and rollback if batch_util drop >3% sustained 30m or kvcache_hitrate drop >5%

deploy-bot: deploy rwd/ks/2026-03-17 v1.2.3 -> canary (p4-12) started by @maria at 2026-03-17T10:00Z :rocket:

Tom Wu: action items:
- Maria: push dashboard panels for the new metrics (batch_stability, kernel_switches/sec, queue_rtt) — add alerting rules.
- Raj: add runtime rule engine fallback prototype to canary agent and ensure cooldown.
- Eva: run synthetic tail-heavy workloads to validate pinned-fused behaviour and measure token/sec delta.
- Tom: draft rollback thresholds and add to rollout doc.

Maria Gonzalez: noted. I’ll upload profiler flame + kvcache trace to the thread in a sec. For now copying the short stack from the profile: 
```
runtime::dispatch_kernel()
  -> kernel_selector::choose_fused_or_split()
  -> attention_kernels::fused::run()
  -> kv_cache::evict_if_conflict()
```

Raj Patel: nice. One more ask — can bench-bot emit a rolling 1h comparison (new vs baseline) every 15m into the channel?

bench-bot: scheduled: hourly stability digest will be posted for rollout rwd/ks/2026-03-17. Next report in ~15m.

Maria Gonzalez: thanks all. If bench report shows sustained regressions we’ll pause rollout and revert selector immediately. :thumbsup:

Tom Wu: sounds good. Low-risk experiment, but lets make observability bulletproof before re-ramp.

Eva Li: I’ll start the tail workload now and post results.

Maria Gonzalez: appreciate it — will follow up with dashboard links and the flame graph attachment.
